items.titulo: Bracco invests $230M in first US diagnostic imaging manufacturing facility
items.resumen: Bracco announced it will invest $230 million to establish its first U.S. manufacturing facility for injectable contrast media in Sanford, North Carolina.

items.titulo: Jazz's $820M Actio buyout gives rise to Setara, armed with $90M series A
items.resumen: Setara Biosciences, a privately held spinout formed following Jazz Pharmaceuticals' acquisition of Actio Biosciences in September, has raised $90 million in series A financing to advance its clinical-stage neuroscience drug candidate and earlier-stage pipeline.

items.titulo: AstraZeneca cuts early-phase prostate cancer pipeline
items.resumen: AstraZeneca has punted a pair of early-phase prostate cancer programs as part of its quarterly pipeline clear out.

items.titulo: Bambusa shoots past IPO targets as Aspen trims offering
items.resumen: Bambusa Therapeutics has upsized its IPO, selling more shares at the midpoint of its target range to gross $168.9 million for bispecific R&D. But Aspen Neuroscience underperformed expectations, hitting the bottom end of its target range and selling slightly fewer shares than expected.

items.titulo: Roche launches differential diagnosis test for mesothelioma
items.resumen: Roche announced the global launch of its VENTANA BAP1 (SP527) test, an automated, ready-to-use immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay.

items.titulo: Sanofi considering ‘moonshot’ treatments as M&A targets to survive Dupixent patent cliff
items.resumen: Sanofi is considering “moonshot” treatments among the potential acquisition targets needed for the French pharma to urgently replenish its pipeline, Chief Financial Officer François-Xavier Roger told Fierce.

items.titulo: Molecular Partners to lay off up to 44% of workforce in radiotherapy pivot
items.resumen: Molecular Partners plans to lay off up to 44% of its staff as it focuses its declining cash reserves on a radiotherapeutic pipeline led by an early-phase small cell lung cancer drug candidate.

items.titulo: Eli Lilly scraps phase 2 Alzheimer's program after drug falls short of expectations
items.resumen: Eli Lilly has dropped its phase 2 Alzheimer's disease program for mevidalen, marking another setback for the experimental drug as the Big Pharma expands its neuroscience pipeline through multibillion-dollar acquisitions.

items.titulo: Merck outlines 2027 as ‘another year of investment’ despite recent clinical wins
items.resumen: Even as a wave of clinical trial wins bolsters its momentum, Merck & Co. is prioritizing ongoing pipeline and commercial expansions over near-term margin growth, hoping to strengthen its long-term prospects past Keytruda's loss of exclusivity.

items.titulo: BMS walks away from $80M neurodegeneration bet after phase 1
items.resumen: Bristol Myers Squibb has scrapped a phase 1 program it bet $80 million on just two years ago.

items.titulo: BioMarin inks up to $475M deal to challenge Fabry ERT incumbents
items.resumen: BioMarin is paying $70 million upfront to license a Fabry disease drug candidate, expanding the franchise it acquired through its $4.8 billion takeover of Amicus Therapeutics.

items.titulo: Flagship brings 3 biotech platforms together to launch AI drug discovery player Etcelera
items.resumen: Flagship Pioneering unveiled Etcelera today, a new AI-powered biotech emerging from stealth that aims to predict how potential medicines will act in patients.

items.resumen: In this tracker, Fierce Pharma is recording the regulatory progress of in-market products, including expansions into key geographies and new indications. Some of these updates may not meet the bar for standalone stories, but we think they are still worth mentioning.

items.titulo: The Oral GLP-1 Tracker: Foundayo, Wegovy pill rally toward previous records

items.titulo: As Dupixent keeps sales churning, Sanofi doubles down on R&D re-work
items.resumen: Amid a push to win back investor confidence in its R&D trajectory, Sanofi still has significant commercial powder to burn with Dupixent, as illustrated in a third-quarter showing that looked strong by the numbers and lifted the French drugmaker’s share price nearly 4% Friday morning.

items.titulo: AstraZeneca launches $1.5B savings plan to fuel pipeline growth, says workforce won't shrink
items.resumen: Facing looming patent cliffs, AstraZeneca has launched a restructuring initiative aimed at saving $1.5 billion annually by 2029. But executives said the overhaul won't result in a net reduction in jobs.

items.titulo: Pfizer looks to reroute supply after flooding sidelined India injectables plant
items.resumen: A Pfizer joint venture with Zydus Cadila in India that manufactures sterile injectables, including chemotherapy drugs for U.S. cancer patients, remains closed after severe flooding in July, with the company estimating that new supplies could begin returning in mid-to-late 2028 under a best-case scenario.
